title: Tlatoāni and Mācron learn to animate
what_the_loop_shows: 48 frames at 12 fps (4 s), looping. In a sunlit greenhouse workshop, tiny Mācron sits on the tabletop behind an open flipbook, drawing. The little red ball on the left page hops up off the paper, bounces three times (each lower) and settles back on the page. Mācron lifts his arms and turns his face up toward Tlatoāni, who sits on a stool beside the table, points at the ball and nods with a calm smile, gills swaying; then Mācron goes back to drawing.
how: A Blender blockout (bpy, headless in the forge) sets the world, the contacts and the motion and renders a depth pass. Wan 2.2 Fun VACE 14B, run headless through studio.queue_workflow in this project's ComfyUI studio, draws all 57 frames in one clip from that depth video and one identity image. A deterministic blend of the 8 overlapping frames closes the loop. Nothing was painted by hand.

tools.blender: bpy 5.3.0 wheel on Python 3.13 (uv), CPU rendering: Workbench (clay, wire) and EEVEE (depth)
tools.pillow: 13.0.0, only for packing frames and the final WebP encoding

prompt: Warm hand-drawn 2D cartoon animation with clean ink outlines and soft sunlit colours, static camera, in a sunlit greenhouse workshop with wooden beams, hanging glass globes and potted plants. A tiny cream robot with a cream body, a small teal chest panel, a dark screen face, two glowing cyan eyes and an antenna orb sits on a wooden table behind an open paper flipbook, always holding a yellow pencil and drawing. On the left page lies a little red ball he drew; it hops up off the page, bounces three times, each lower, and lands back on the page; the robot throws up his arms in delight and turns to look up, then goes back to drawing. Beside the table, a pink axolotl with feathery coral gills, a cream tunic with teal trim and one tail sits on a wooden stool, points at the ball and nods with a calm smile, gills gently swaying. Smooth, gentle, friendly motion.
negative_prompt: camera movement, zoom, cut, flicker, morphing, melting, distorted face, extra limbs, extra robots, extra characters, red light on robot, mustache, beard, second tail, 3d render, grey clay, text, watermark, scary, angry, blurry, low quality, static

steps.what: Build the world and the 48-frame cyclic motion; render wire, clay and depth passes at 640x480.
steps.cpu_time: about 5.5 min for 144 renders on 20 cores

steps.what: Pack 57 depth frames (frame i = depth i mod 48) and an all-white mask as multi-frame PNGs, which core LoadImage reads as image batches.

One Wan 2.2 Fun VACE run: depth video as control, identity-reference.png as the reference image, 640x480, 57 frames, 20 steps split 10/10 between the high- and low-noise experts, cfg 3.5, shift 8, euler/simple.
steps.gpu_time: about 10 min on an RTX A5000 (warm)

steps.what: Frames 48-56 redraw the moments of frames 0-8 in the same run. Blend frame 48+k into frame k for k < 8 (weights rising from 1/9 to 8/9 toward the first drawing). The overlap is a quiet beat (Mācron drawing, ball at rest), so this evens out line shimmer and never mixes two poses.
Encode the final and the breakdown loops as lossy WebP at 12 fps.

identity_reference_provenance: identity-reference.png is frame 0 of an earlier Wan VACE pass (seed 21, same workflow and prompt, 49 frames) driven by the previous blockout state: before the pencil and Mācron's arms were thickened so the depth pass shows them. That pass in turn used the v1 keyframe (below) as its reference.

attempts_that_did_not_ship.what: Two-image Qwen-Image-Edit keyframe (picture 1: the v1 keyframe; picture 2: the Blender clay render)
attempts_that_did_not_ship.why: Both drew two robots and kept picture 1's table: picture and control disagreed, so the model drew both (kumbia-kombat lesson A5).

attempts_that_did_not_ship.what: VACE from depth, ball on the right page next to Mācron
attempts_that_did_not_ship.why: The ball merged into Mācron as a red chest light, and the first hop flew to the top of the frame. The ball moved to the left page, clear of him, and the hops were lowered.

attempts_that_did_not_ship.what: Pinning one frame at both ends (mask black) to force the loop closed
attempts_that_did_not_ship.why: Wan's VAE packs frames in groups of four, and a lone kept frame is redrawn, not copied: the ends still differed by 4.0. Mācron's pencil came and went, because at 6 mm it did not show in the depth pass.

attempts_that_did_not_ship.what: A 25-frame bridge regenerating the seam between 9 + 8 kept frames
attempts_that_did_not_ship.why: Kept frames are redrawn too (they differ by 5-6 from their inputs), so splicing two runs made two jumps (6.9 and 12.8). Generating past the cycle in one run and blending the overlap worked instead.

attempts_that_did_not_ship.what: v1 (published first in PR #2): four Qwen-Image-Edit pose edits of one keyframe in ping-pong order
attempts_that_did_not_ship.why: Each frame was an independent edit, so details shimmered and the motion jumped. The operator rejected it, rightly. Its keyframe (Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 + Lightning, seed 101, from 'Quote Anchors Hold', sha256 ab577ee7…) is still the root of this loop's identity.
